question.text: What will be the ending value of the ICE BofA US High Yield Option-Adjusted Spread for these biweekly periods of Q4 2026? (Nov 9-20 (wider range))
question.resolution_criteria: Each subquestion will resolve as the last available daily value of the ICE BofA US High Yield OAS published on the [FRED website](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/BAMLH0A0HYM2) for the final calendar day (typically the final Friday) of the corresponding biweekly period.
question.fine_print:
* If the FRED data is delayed, the value will be taken as soon as published for the relevant date.
* If the market is closed on the scheduled ending date or if no value for that date is published by FRED for two weeks, the most recent available value from an earlier day in the period will be used.
* Only the initially published value for each date will be used (no revisions).
* The value is reported in percentage points.

- The question resolves on the value for Friday 2026-11-20, which FRED will normally publish on Nov 23 (one business day later).

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. The spread sits at 3.44, the widest level in the recent run. It has risen about 78 bp since the 2.66 low on Sep 21 and is near the middle of the question's 1.745 to 4.255 range.

[FXStreet](https://www.fxstreet.com/analysis/why-is-gold-falling-alongside-tech-stocks-a-closer-look-at-liquidity-and-the-bond-market-202611020135)

[MarketsFN](https://www.marketsfn.com/article/credit-spreads-daily-2026-10-27), [Lead-Lag](https://www.leadlagreport.com/junk-bonds-split-in-two-ccc-spreads-are-wider-than-april-2025/), [TPFG](https://www.tpfg.com/marketinsights/chart-of-the-week-10.26.26)

- 2026-10-09: CNBC said junk bonds were "flashing yellow", with spreads at their widest since April. A Morgan Stanley strategist called the moves "orderly". [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/09/junk-bonds-are-flashing-yellow-watch-these-warning-signs.html)

## 4. Base rates
- Statistical baseline from the provided code: 14 trading days of changes since 2005, with the last 3 years weighted double, applied to 3.44. Percentiles: p5 3.05, p10 3.16, p25 3.30, **p50 3.40**, p75 3.53, p90 3.70, p95 3.83.
- Recent volatility is high. Daily moves of 10 to 18 bp were common in October (+18 on 10-30, +13 on 10-22, -12 on 10-26, -14 on 10-01 to 10-02). The October range was 3.03 to 3.44, a 41 bp spread.
- The trend over two months is widening: roughly 2.65 to 2.70 in early September, 3.1 to 3.2 in early October, 3.44 by Oct 30.
- For context, the April 2025 tariff shock peaked at about 4.61 (Katusa). [Katusa](https://katusaresearch.com/high-yield-spread/) The 10-year average is about 3.83.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on the HY OAS.
- The collected Kalshi and Polymarket markets cover Treasury yields only, so they are only indirectly relevant. Kalshi prices the 30-year yield reaching at least 5.39% by Nov 30 at about 50%. Polymarket prices the 10-year reaching 5.5% before 2027 at about 9.6%. Several of the collected markets show prices of 0 or 1, which suggests they are stale or already resolved.
- I found no published sell-side point forecasts for HY OAS in mid-November.

## 6. Upcoming events before Nov 20

- About 2026-11-17/18: Nvidia FQ3 earnings, unconfirmed. Calendars disagree between Nov 17, Nov 18 and Nov 25. This is a key event for the AI-driven risk sentiment behind the current widening. [CME Elite](https://www.cmelitegroup.com/knowledge-hub/nvidia-earnings-date/), [EarningsWhispers](https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/Nvda)
- No FOMC meeting falls in the window. I could not verify the date, but the next decision is reportedly Dec 9. [eco3min](https://eco3min.fr/en/macro-calendar/)
- Other things to watch: whether the AI/data-center and neocloud selloff continues, CCC stress and default headlines, HY fund flows, and contagion from China property credit (Huafa).

I could not find any HY OAS reading for Nov 2 beyond FRED's Oct 30 value.

- I found no published sell-side point forecast for HY OAS in late November 2026. On Oct 29, BofA recommended buying Argentine debt, which is not directly relevant. [Cronista](https://www.cronista.com/finanzas-mercados/bancos-de-wall-street-recomiendan-comprar-argentina-pero-la-demanda-aun-no-aparece-que-pasa/)

- Around Nov 10-13: October CPI, which matters given the hot September CPI and the risk of a December hike.
- 2026-11-11: Veterans Day, a bond-market holiday.
- Around Nov 18: October FOMC minutes. [Admiral Markets](https://admiralmarkets.com/analytics/traders-blog/fomc-minutes-october-2026)
- Mid to late November: Nvidia earnings, probably around Nov 18-19 (date not verified). These are key to the AI-spending sentiment behind the recent tech and credit selloff.
- Ongoing: heavy AI-related debt supply (Oracle's $20B raise, Marvell/Lumentum deal financing), Iran diplomacy and oil prices, and stress in CCC-rated and AI "neocloud" credits.

(e) Historically, the spread moves over 14 trading days with p5 to p95 of about -39 to +39 bp, centred near zero, with a slight right skew. Current daily volatility is elevated, with 10 to 18 bp moves common, so the tails should be somewhat wider than the baseline.

- **Low:** A benign jobs report and CPI, plus strong Nvidia earnings around Nov 18, revive AI risk appetite. Spreads then retrace toward 3.0 to 3.1.
- **High:** The AI capex selloff deepens, CCC defaults or a neocloud credit event occur, and China property contagion spreads. Spreads then blow out toward 4.2 to 4.6, similar to the April 2025 peak of about 4.61.
